records.source: Καὶ ὅτε ἤγγισαν εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα καὶ ἦλθον εἰς Βηθφαγὴ εἰς τὸ Ὄρος τῶν Ἐλαιῶν, τότε Ἰησοῦς ἀπέστειλεν δύο μαθητὰς λέγων αὐτοῖς· Πορεύεσθε εἰς τὴν κώμην τὴν κατέναντι ὑμῶν, καὶ εὐθέως εὑρήσετε ὄνον δεδεμένην καὶ πῶλον μετ’ αὐτῆς· λύσαντες ἀγάγετέ μοι.
records.gloss: And when they drew near to Jerusalem and came to Bethphage to the Mount of the Olives, then Jesus sent two disciples, \v 2 saying to them, Go into the village the opposite you, and immediately you will find a donkey having been tied and a colt with her; having untied bring to me.
pieces: When they were getting close to Jerusalem and had come to Bethphage on the Mount of Olives, Jesus sent two disciples on ahead
with instructions: "Go into the village across from you, and straightaway you will come upon a donkey tied up there with her colt. Untie them and lead them to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

L.1: And when they drew near to Jerusalem and came to Bethphage, to the Mount of Olives, then Jesus sent two disciples,
L.2: saying to them, "Go into the village opposite you, and at once you will find a donkey tied [there], and a colt with her; untie [them and] bring [them] to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

R.1: Jesus and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} followers were coming near Jerusalem. They came to the village of Bethphage at the Mount of Olives. Then Jesus sent two of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} followers ahead.
R.2: He told them, "Go into the village in front of you. Right away you will find a donkey tied up there, with her young colt beside her. Untie them and bring them to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

decisions.choice: Bethphage, at the Mount of Olives: a village on the hill east of Jerusalem
decisions.reason: The Mount of Olives faces Jerusalem across the Kidron Valley. Bethphage lay on its slope, on the road from Jericho, so Jesus enters the city from the east.

decisions.choice: the Mount of Olives: the place where Zechariah sees the LORD come to his city
decisions.reason: Zechariah 14:4 pictures the LORD standing on the Mount of Olives on the day he comes. The same prophet is quoted in 21:5.

decisions.choice: colt: a young donkey, the foal of the donkey that is tied
decisions.reason: The word means the young of an animal. Here it is the donkey's foal, as 21:5 makes clear.

decisions.choice: Jesus and his followers
decisions.reason: Readable names who was traveling, because the scene opens a new section.

records.heading: The king comes to Jerusalem on a donkey

records.source: καὶ ἐάν τις ὑμῖν εἴπῃ τι, ἐρεῖτε ὅτι Ὁ κύριος αὐτῶν χρείαν ἔχει· εὐθὺς δὲ ἀποστελεῖ αὐτούς.
records.gloss: And if anyone to you says anything, you will say that The Lord of them need has; immediately then he will send them.
pieces: If anyone questions you, say, 'The Lord needs them.' Then he will let them go at once."

L.3: And if anyone says anything to you, you will say, 'The Lord has need of them,' and immediately he will send them."

R.3: If anyone asks you about it, say, 'The Lord needs them.' Then the owner will let you take them right away."

decisions.choice: the Lord: Jesus speaks of himself
decisions.reason: Matthew uses this title for Jesus in the mouth of those who trust him (8:2; 8:25). The owner's consent shows that he recognizes the claim.

decisions.choice: of them: goes with need (he has need of them)
decisions.reason: The pronoun can go with "the Lord" or with "need". The sense "their master needs them" would make the owner the speaker's lord, which does not fit the story.

decisions.choice: he will send them: the owner will let the animals go at once
alternatives: Jesus will send them back promptly
decisions.reason: Mark 11:3 has a similar line that may mean Jesus will return the colt. In Matthew the subject is most naturally the person who asks.

decisions.choice: the owner
decisions.reason: Readable says who will let the animals go.

records.source: Τοῦτο δὲ γέγονεν ἵνα πληρωθῇ τὸ ῥηθὲν διὰ τοῦ προφήτου λέγοντος·
records.gloss: This then came to pass so that might be fulfilled the having been spoken through the prophet saying,
pieces: This happened so that the word spoken through the prophet would be fulfilled:

L.4: Now this has happened so that what was spoken through the prophet might be fulfilled, saying:

R.4: This made what the prophet had said come true:

decisions.choice: the prophet: Zechariah, whose words follow, opened with a line of Isaiah
decisions.reason: The words of 21:5 are Zechariah 9:9, introduced by a phrase from Isaiah 62:11. Matthew names no prophet here.

decisions.choice: the same wording as 1:22, 2:15 and 4:14
decisions.reason: The formula that introduces a fulfilled prophecy is given in the same words each time.

records.source: Εἴπατε τῇ θυγατρὶ Σιών· Ἰδοὺ ὁ βασιλεύς σου ἔρχεταί σοι πραῢς καὶ ἐπιβεβηκὼς ἐπὶ ὄνον καὶ ἐπὶ πῶλον υἱὸν ὑποζυγίου.
records.gloss: Say to the daughter of Zion, Behold the king of you comes to you, gentle and having mounted on a donkey and on a colt a son of a beast of burden.
pieces: "Tell the daughter of Zion, 'Your king is coming to you! He is gentle, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is seated on a donkey and on a colt, the foal of a pack animal.'"

L.5: "Say to the daughter of Zion, 'Look, your king is coming to you, gentle and mounted on a donkey, and on a colt, [the] foal of a beast of burden.'"

R.5: "Tell the people of Jerusalem, 'Look! Your king is coming to you. He is gentle. He is riding on a donkey and on a young donkey, a colt.'"

decisions.choice: Isaiah 62:11 and Zechariah 9:9
decisions.reason: "Say to the daughter of Zion" opens Isaiah 62:11; the rest is Zechariah 9:9. Matthew leaves out Zechariah's words about the king being righteous and bringing salvation, and keeps the word gentle.

decisions.choice: the daughter of Zion: Jerusalem and its people
alternatives: a young woman of the city
decisions.reason: The prophets speak of a city as a daughter. Zion is the hill of the temple and stands for the whole city.

decisions.choice: gentle: meek, not proud or violent
decisions.reason: It is the word of 5:5 and 11:29. A king who comes on a donkey, not a war horse, comes in peace (Zechariah 9:10).

decisions.choice: on a donkey and on a colt: Matthew names two animals
decisions.reason: In Hebrew poetry the second line names the same donkey again. Matthew's story has two animals (21:2, 7) and reads the words that way.

decisions.choice: look (L, R); not rendered (B)
decisions.reason: Literal and Readable keep the call to look; Balanced carries its force with an exclamation.

decisions.choice: spans on he for the king
decisions.reason: The king is Jesus, so pronouns for him take the deity_pronoun setting, as with the servant in 12:18-21.

decisions.choice: the people of Jerusalem
decisions.reason: Readable says who is meant.

records.source: πορευθέντες δὲ οἱ μαθηταὶ καὶ ποιήσαντες καθὼς συνέταξεν αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἤγαγον τὴν ὄνον καὶ τὸν πῶλον, καὶ ἐπέθηκαν ἐπ’ αὐτῶν τὰ ἱμάτια, καὶ ἐπεκάθισεν ἐπάνω αὐτῶν.
records.gloss: Having gone then the disciples and having done as directed them the Jesus \v 7 they brought the donkey and the colt, and they put on them the cloaks, and he sat on them.
pieces: The disciples went off and did what Jesus had told them.
They brought the donkey and the colt and laid their cloaks on them, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} sat on them.

L.6: And the disciples went and did just as Jesus had directed them;
L.7: they brought the donkey and the colt and put their cloaks on them, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} sat on them.

R.6: The two followers went and did what Jesus had told them to do.
R.7: They brought the donkey and the colt to Jesus. They put their coats on the animals, and Jesus sat on them.

decisions.choice: he sat on them: most likely on the cloaks laid over the animals
decisions.reason: The nearest plural is the cloaks. Matthew does not say how Jesus rode; the words need not mean he sat on two animals.

decisions.choice: cloaks: the outer garments, laid on as a saddle
decisions.reason: The disciples use their own outer clothing to make a seat, an act of honor.

decisions.choice: on the animals; Jesus
decisions.reason: Readable makes clear what the cloaks were put on and who sat.

records.source: ὁ δὲ πλεῖστος ὄχλος ἔστρωσαν ἑαυτῶν τὰ ἱμάτια ἐν τῇ ὁδῷ, ἄλλοι δὲ ἔκοπτον κλάδους ἀπὸ τῶν δένδρων καὶ ἐστρώννυον ἐν τῇ ὁδῷ.
records.gloss: The then very large crowd spread their own the cloaks on the road, others then were cutting branches from the trees and were spreading on the road.
pieces: The crowd, which was very large, spread their own cloaks across the road, and others kept cutting branches from the trees and laying them on the road.

L.8: And the very large crowd spread their own cloaks on the road, and others were cutting branches from the trees and spreading [them] on the road.

R.8: The huge crowd spread their coats on the road. Other people cut branches from the trees and spread them on the road too.

decisions.choice: the very large crowd
decisions.reason: The word is a superlative. With a group it can mean the greater part of it; here it more likely describes the size of the crowd.

decisions.choice: cloaks spread on the road: a welcome for a king
alternatives: a way to keep the dust down
decisions.reason: When Jehu was made king, the people spread their cloaks under him (2 Kings 9:13). Branches were waved at festivals and victories (1 Maccabees 13:51).

decisions.choice: coats
decisions.reason: Readable uses a common word for an outer garment.

records.source: οἱ δὲ ὄχλοι οἱ προάγοντες αὐτὸν καὶ οἱ ἀκολουθοῦντες ἔκραζον λέγοντες· Ὡσαννὰ τῷ υἱῷ Δαυίδ· Εὐλογημένος ὁ ἐρχόμενος ἐν ὀνόματι κυρίου· Ὡσαννὰ ἐν τοῖς ὑψίστοις.
records.gloss: The then crowds the going before him and the following were crying out saying, Hosanna to the son of David; blessed the coming in name of Lord; Hosanna in the highest.
pieces: Crowds walked in front of {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and behind {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and they kept shouting, "Hosanna to the Son of David! Blessed is the one who comes in the name of the Lord! Hosanna in the highest heavens!"

L.9: And the crowds going ahead of {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and those following were crying out, saying, "Hosanna to the Son of David! Blessed [is] the one coming in [the] name of [the] Lord! Hosanna in the highest!"

R.9: Crowds of people walked ahead of Jesus and behind {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. They were shouting, "Hosanna to the Son of David! May God bless the one who comes in the name of the Lord! Hosanna to God in heaven!"

decisions.choice: Hosanna: a Hebrew cry meaning save, please, used as a shout of praise
alternatives: a simple cheer with no meaning
decisions.reason: The word comes from Psalm 118:25, "save us, please". Sung at the great feasts, it had become a cry of praise and welcome as well as a prayer.

decisions.choice: blessed is the one who comes in the name of the Lord: Psalm 118:26
decisions.reason: The psalm was sung by pilgrims going up to the temple. Where Matthew has "Lord", the Hebrew has God's name, the LORD. The crowds apply the words to Jesus as the king who comes.

decisions.choice: Son of David: the king promised from David's family
decisions.reason: God promised David a son whose kingdom would last forever (2 Samuel 7:12-16). The crowds hail Jesus as that king (see 1:1; 12:23).

decisions.choice: in the highest: in the highest heavens, where God is
decisions.reason: The cry calls on God in heaven, or on those in heaven to join the praise (Psalm 148:1-2).

decisions.choice: Hosanna at every level
decisions.reason: The word is a cry of both prayer and praise. Every level keeps it, and the meaning decision explains it.

decisions.choice: May God bless the one who comes; to God in heaven
alternatives: Blessed is the one coming; in the highest
decisions.reason: Readable says who blesses and where the praise is directed.

records.source: καὶ εἰσελθόντος αὐτοῦ εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα ἐσείσθη πᾶσα ἡ πόλις λέγουσα· Τίς ἐστιν οὗτος;
records.gloss: And having entered of him into Jerusalem was stirred all the city saying, Who is this?
pieces: When {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} came into Jerusalem, the whole city was in an uproar. "Who is this man?" people asked.

L.10: And when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} entered Jerusalem, the whole city was shaken, saying, "Who is this?"

R.10: When Jesus went into Jerusalem, everyone in the city was stirred up. They asked, "Who is this man?"

decisions.choice: was shaken: stirred up, in turmoil
decisions.reason: The verb is used of an earthquake (27:51; 28:4). All Jerusalem was troubled in the same way when the magi asked about the king (2:3).

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: Readable names Jesus.

records.source: οἱ δὲ ὄχλοι ἔλεγον· Οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ προφήτης Ἰησοῦς ὁ ἀπὸ Ναζαρὲθ τῆς Γαλιλαίας.
records.gloss: The then crowds were saying, This is the prophet Jesus the from Nazareth of Galilee.
pieces: And the crowds kept saying, "This is the prophet, Jesus, the man from Nazareth in Galilee."

L.11: And the crowds were saying, "This is the prophet Jesus, the one from Nazareth of Galilee."

R.11: The crowds said, "This is Jesus, the prophet. He comes from the town of Nazareth in Galilee."

decisions.choice: the prophet: a prophet sent by God, perhaps the prophet Moses promised
decisions.reason: The crowds hold Jesus to be a prophet (21:46). The article may point to the prophet like Moses (Deuteronomy 18:15), but the crowds may mean no more than a known prophet.

decisions.choice: from Nazareth of Galilee: his hometown in the north
decisions.reason: Jesus grew up in Nazareth (2:23). The pilgrims from Galilee name him by his town.

records.source: Καὶ εἰσῆλθεν Ἰησοῦς εἰς τὸ ἱερόν, καὶ ἐξέβαλεν πάντας τοὺς πωλοῦντας καὶ ἀγοράζοντας ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ καὶ τὰς τραπέζας τῶν κολλυβιστῶν κατέστρεψεν καὶ τὰς καθέδρας τῶν πωλούντων τὰς περιστεράς, καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς· Γέγραπται· Ὁ οἶκός μου οἶκος προσευχῆς κληθήσεται, ὑμεῖς δὲ αὐτὸν ποιεῖτε σπήλαιον λῃστῶν.
records.gloss: And entered Jesus into the temple and cast out all the selling and buying in the temple, and the tables of the money changers he overturned and the seats of the selling the doves, \v 13 and he says to them, It has been written, The house of me a house of prayer will be called, you but it are making a den of robbers.
pieces: Jesus went into the temple courts and drove out everyone who was buying and selling there. He turned over the tables of the money changers and the seats of the dove sellers.
"It is written," {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} told them, "'My house will be called a house of prayer.' But you are turning it into a hideout for robbers."

L.12: And Jesus entered the temple and threw out all those selling and buying in the temple, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} overturned the tables of the money changers and the seats of those selling the doves,
L.13: and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} says to them, "It is written, 'My house will be called a house of prayer,' but you are making it a den of robbers."

R.12: Then Jesus went into the temple area. He forced out all the people who were buying and selling things there. He turned over the tables of the men who exchanged money. He also turned over the seats of the people who sold doves.
R.13: He said to them, "The Scriptures say, 'My house will be called a house of prayer.' But you are making it a place where robbers hide."

decisions.choice: the temple: the courts around the sanctuary
decisions.reason: The word means the whole temple area. The trading took place in the large outer court, open to Gentiles.

decisions.choice: money changers and dove sellers: trades that served the offerings
decisions.reason: Worshipers paid the temple tax in a set coin (17:24), so other money had to be exchanged. Doves were the offering of the poor (Leviticus 5:7; 12:8).

decisions.choice: Isaiah 56:7 and Jeremiah 7:11
decisions.reason: In Isaiah 56:7 God calls the temple a house of prayer for all peoples. In Jeremiah 7:11 God asks whether his house has become a den of robbers, a place where wrongdoers hide and feel safe.

decisions.choice: the temple, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: the temple of God, the reading of many manuscripts
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts read "the temple of God"; several early ones do not. The meaning is the same. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: My at the start of the quotation, with no span
decisions.reason: God speaks in the quoted words, so "my" would take the deity_pronoun setting; at the start of a sentence it is capitalized either way.

decisions.choice: present tense of narration (L); past (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek present tense of narration.

decisions.choice: hideout for robbers (B); place where robbers hide (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what a den of robbers was: a hiding place for bandits.

records.heading: Jesus clears the temple

records.source: Καὶ προσῆλθον αὐτῷ τυφλοὶ καὶ χωλοὶ ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ, καὶ ἐθεράπευσεν αὐτούς.
records.gloss: And came to him blind and lame in the temple, and he healed them.
pieces: Blind and lame people came to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} in the temple courts, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} healed them.

L.14: And blind and lame [people] came to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} in the temple, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} healed them.

R.14: People who were blind or could not walk came to Jesus in the temple area, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} healed them.

decisions.choice: the blind and the lame in the temple: welcomed where they were once kept out
decisions.reason: A saying from David's time kept the blind and lame from the house (2 Samuel 5:8), and the law barred priests with such defects from serving (Leviticus 21:18). Jesus, the Son of David, heals them in the temple.

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: Readable names Jesus.

records.source: ἰδόντες δὲ οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ οἱ γραμματεῖς τὰ θαυμάσια ἃ ἐποίησεν καὶ τοὺς παῖδας τοὺς κράζοντας ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ καὶ λέγοντας· Ὡσαννὰ τῷ υἱῷ Δαυίδ ἠγανάκτησαν καὶ εἶπαν αὐτῷ· Ἀκούεις τί οὗτοι λέγουσιν;
records.gloss: Having seen then the chief priests and the scribes the wonders that he did and the children the crying out in the temple and saying, Hosanna to the son of David, they were indignant \v 16 and said to him, Hear you what these say?
pieces: The chief priests and the scribes saw the amazing things {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was doing, and they saw the children shouting in the temple courts, "Hosanna to the Son of David!" They were furious,
and they said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Do {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} hear what these children are saying?"

L.15: But when the chief priests and the scribes saw the wonders that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} did, and the children crying out in the temple and saying, "Hosanna to the Son of David," they were indignant,
L.16: and they said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Do {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} hear what these are saying?"

R.15: The leading priests and the teachers of the law saw the wonderful things Jesus did. They also saw the children shouting in the temple area, "Hosanna to the Son of David!" This made the leaders very angry.
R.16: They said to Jesus, "Do {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} hear what these children are saying?"

decisions.choice: wonders: the healings just done
decisions.reason: The word means remarkable deeds. It refers back to the healing of the blind and lame (21:14).

decisions.choice: children: boys and girls, young enough to be called infants in 21:16
decisions.reason: The word can mean child or servant. Jesus answers with a verse about infants, so children are meant.

decisions.choice: do you hear: a demand that Jesus stop them
decisions.reason: The leaders expect Jesus to reject the title the children give him.

decisions.choice: leading priests; teachers of the law
decisions.reason: Readable uses the plain names used in 2:4.

records.source: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς λέγει αὐτοῖς· Ναί.
records.gloss: The but Jesus says to them, Yes.
pieces: Jesus answered them, "I do.

decisions.choice: present tense of narration (L); past (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek present tense of narration.

decisions.choice: I do (B); Yes, I hear them (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable answer the question in full.

records.source: οὐδέποτε ἀνέγνωτε ὅτι Ἐκ στόματος νηπίων καὶ θηλαζόντων κατηρτίσω αἶνον;
records.gloss: Never did you read that Out of mouth of infants and nursing you prepared for yourself praise?
pieces: Did you never read this: 'Out of the mouths of little children and nursing babies {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have brought forth praise for {{deity_pronoun:yourself|Yourself}}'?"

L.16: Have you never read, 'Out of [the] mouth of infants and nursing [babies] {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have prepared praise for {{deity_pronoun:yourself|Yourself}}'?"

R.16: Surely you have read this in the Scriptures: 'You have made little children and babies sing {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} praise.'"

decisions.choice: Psalm 8:2 (8:3 in the Hebrew numbering), in the Greek Old Testament
decisions.reason: Jesus quotes the Greek version, which has "praise" where the Hebrew has "strength". In the psalm God is addressed; Jesus applies the words to the children praising him.

decisions.choice: have you never read: a question that expects yes
decisions.reason: The scribes knew the psalm. Jesus asks whether they have seen what it means, as in 12:3 and 19:4.

decisions.choice: prepared: brought about, made complete
decisions.reason: The verb means to put in order or make ready; with the middle voice, for oneself.

decisions.choice: spans on you and yourself for God
decisions.reason: The psalm speaks to God, so the pronouns take the deity_pronoun setting.

decisions.choice: a statement instead of a question
decisions.reason: The question expects yes; Readable states it, as at other such questions.

records.source: καὶ καταλιπὼν αὐτοὺς ἐξῆλθεν ἔξω τῆς πόλεως εἰς Βηθανίαν, καὶ ηὐλίσθη ἐκεῖ.
records.gloss: And having left them he went out outside the city to Bethany, and he lodged there.
pieces: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} left them and went out of the city to Bethany, where {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} spent the night.

L.17: And leaving them, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} went out of the city to Bethany, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} spent the night there.

R.17: Then Jesus left them. He went out of the city to the village of Bethany and stayed there for the night.

decisions.choice: Bethany: a village on the far side of the Mount of Olives
decisions.reason: Bethany lay about two miles from Jerusalem (John 11:18). Pilgrims at the feasts often lodged outside the crowded city.

decisions.choice: Jesus; the village of
decisions.reason: Readable names Jesus and says what Bethany was.

records.source: Πρωῒ δὲ ἐπανάγων εἰς τὴν πόλιν ἐπείνασεν.
records.gloss: Early then returning into the city he was hungry.
pieces: Early in the morning, as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was going back into the city, Jesus felt hungry.

L.18: Now early in the morning, as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was returning to the city, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was hungry.

R.18: Early the next morning, Jesus was going back to the city. He was hungry.

decisions.choice: early: in the early morning, before full daylight
decisions.reason: The word is used of the last part of the night and the first hours of day.

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: A new scene begins, so Balanced and Readable name Jesus.

records.heading: The fig tree with nothing but leaves

records.source: καὶ ἰδὼν συκῆν μίαν ἐπὶ τῆς ὁδοῦ ἦλθεν ἐπ’ αὐτήν, καὶ οὐδὲν εὗρεν ἐν αὐτῇ εἰ μὴ φύλλα μόνον, καὶ λέγει αὐτῇ· Μηκέτι ἐκ σοῦ καρπὸς γένηται εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα· καὶ ἐξηράνθη παραχρῆμα ἡ συκῆ.
records.gloss: And having seen fig tree one by the road he came to it, and nothing found on it if not leaves only, and he says to it, No longer from you fruit may be into the age. And withered immediately the fig tree.
pieces: Seeing a fig tree beside the road, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} went up to it, but {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} found nothing on it except leaves. Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to it, "From now on, may no fruit ever grow on you!" At once the fig tree dried up.

L.19: And seeing a single fig tree by the road, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} went to it and found nothing on it except leaves only, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} says to it, "May fruit no longer come from you, forever." And the fig tree withered at once.

R.19: Jesus saw a fig tree beside the road. He went to it to find some figs, but there was nothing on it except leaves. So {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to the tree, "No fruit will ever grow on you again!" Right away the fig tree dried up.

decisions.choice: nothing but leaves: a tree in leaf that promised fruit and had none
alternatives: a tree out of season with no promise of fruit
decisions.reason: Fig trees put out small early figs with their leaves in spring. A tree full of leaves but bare of these had nothing to give.

decisions.choice: the withering: an acted sign of judgment on a fruitless people
alternatives: an act of anger at the tree
decisions.reason: The prophets picture Israel as a fig tree that God finds without fruit (Jeremiah 8:13; Micah 7:1). Matthew places the sign beside the temple scene and the parables about fruit (21:34, 41, 43).

decisions.choice: one: a single tree standing alone
decisions.reason: The word can mean only "a", but it may point to one tree by itself along the road.

decisions.choice: may no fruit come from you: a curse, spoken as a wish
decisions.reason: The verb is a wish or command in form. It takes effect at once.

decisions.choice: present tense of narration (L); past (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek present tense of narration.

decisions.choice: to find some figs; will (for may)
decisions.reason: Readable says why Jesus went to the tree, as 21:18 implies, and gives the curse as a firm statement.

records.source: καὶ ἰδόντες οἱ μαθηταὶ ἐθαύμασαν λέγοντες· Πῶς παραχρῆμα ἐξηράνθη ἡ συκῆ;
records.gloss: And having seen the disciples marveled saying, How immediately withered the fig tree?
pieces: The disciples were astonished when they saw this. "How did the fig tree dry up so quickly?" they asked.

L.20: And when the disciples saw [it], they marveled, saying, "How did the fig tree wither at once?"

R.20: The followers saw this and were amazed. They asked, "How did the fig tree dry up so fast?"

decisions.choice: how so quickly: amazement at the speed
decisions.reason: The disciples ask how it could happen at once, not why Jesus did it.

records.source: ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν, ἐὰν ἔχητε πίστιν καὶ μὴ διακριθῆτε, οὐ μόνον τὸ τῆς συκῆς ποιήσετε, ἀλλὰ κἂν τῷ ὄρει τούτῳ εἴπητε· Ἄρθητι καὶ βλήθητι εἰς τὴν θάλασσαν, γενήσεται·
records.gloss: Answering then the Jesus said to them, Truly I say to you, if you have faith and not doubt, not only the of the fig tree you will do, but even if to the mountain this you say, Be taken up and be cast into the sea, it will happen;
pieces: Jesus answered them, "Truly I tell you, if you have faith and do not doubt, you will do more than what was done to this fig tree. Even if you tell this mountain, 'Be lifted up and thrown into the sea,' it will be done.

L.21: And answering, Jesus said to them, "Truly I tell you, if you have faith and do not doubt, not only will you do what [was done to] the fig tree, but even if you say to this mountain, 'Be lifted up and thrown into the sea,' it will happen.

R.21: Jesus answered, "I tell you the truth. If you have faith and do not doubt, you will be able to do what was done to this fig tree. And you will do even more. You could say to this mountain, 'Be lifted up and thrown into the sea,' and it would happen.

decisions.choice: faith and not doubting: trust in God that does not waver
decisions.reason: To doubt is to be divided, wavering between trust and distrust. Jesus spoke of faith that moves a mountain in 17:20 too.

decisions.choice: moving a mountain: doing what seems impossible
alternatives: a literal plan to move hills
decisions.reason: Removing mountains was a picture of the impossible (Isaiah 40:4; Zechariah 4:7). Jesus speaks with the same picture in 17:20.

decisions.choice: this mountain: probably the Mount of Olives
decisions.reason: They are walking from Bethany over the Mount of Olives to the city. From there the Dead Sea can be seen. Some see the temple mount meant.

decisions.choice: be lifted up and thrown: God is the one who acts
decisions.reason: The passive leaves the actor unnamed; it is God who answers faith.

decisions.choice: the fig tree first, then even more
decisions.reason: Readable breaks the long comparison into short sentences.

records.source: καὶ πάντα ὅσα ἂν αἰτήσητε ἐν τῇ προσευχῇ πιστεύοντες λήμψεσθε.
records.gloss: And all things as many as if you ask in the prayer believing you will receive.
pieces: And everything you ask for in prayer you will receive, as long as you believe."

L.22: And all things whatever you ask in prayer, believing, you will receive."

R.22: When you pray and believe, you will receive anything you ask for."

decisions.choice: whatever you ask, believing: prayer that trusts God the Father
alternatives: a promise to grant any wish
decisions.reason: Jesus has taught his disciples to pray for God's will to be done (6:10) and promised that the Father gives good things (7:11). The promise is made to that kind of trust.

decisions.choice: believing: the condition under which they ask
decisions.reason: The participle describes the asking: those who ask while trusting God.

records.source: Καὶ ἐλθόντος αὐτοῦ εἰς τὸ ἱερὸν προσῆλθον αὐτῷ διδάσκοντι οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ οἱ πρεσβύτεροι τοῦ λαοῦ λέγοντες· Ἐν ποίᾳ ἐξουσίᾳ ταῦτα ποιεῖς;
records.gloss: And having come of him into the temple came to him teaching the chief priests and the elders of the people saying, By what authority these things are you doing?
pieces: Jesus went into the temple courts, and while {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was teaching, the chief priests and the elders of the people came up to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. "What authority do {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have for doing these things?" they asked.

L.23: And when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had come into the temple, the chief priests and the elders of the people came to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was teaching, saying, "By what authority are {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} doing these things?

R.23: Jesus went into the temple area and began to teach. The leading priests and the older leaders of the people came to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. They asked, "What right do {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have to do these things?

decisions.choice: the chief priests and the elders of the people: the leaders of the temple and the nation
decisions.reason: The chief priests ran the temple, and the elders were heads of leading families. With the scribes they made up the council (16:21).

decisions.choice: these things: his entry, the clearing of the temple, his healing and teaching there
decisions.reason: The leaders ask who gave him the right to act as he has in the temple since 21:12.

decisions.choice: authority: the right to act, given by someone
decisions.reason: The question is who gave Jesus the right, as the next sentence makes plain.

decisions.choice: the question closes this sentence; the second question follows
decisions.reason: Balanced puts "they asked" after the first question, and the next record gives the second.

decisions.choice: right
decisions.reason: Readable uses a plain word for the right to act.

records.heading: Who gave Jesus this authority?

records.source: καὶ τίς σοι ἔδωκεν τὴν ἐξουσίαν ταύτην;
records.gloss: And who to you gave the authority this?
pieces: "And who gave {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} this authority?"

decisions.choice: who gave you: the second question presses the first
decisions.reason: The leaders want Jesus to name the source of his authority, which they claim to control in the temple.

records.source: ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Ἐρωτήσω ὑμᾶς κἀγὼ λόγον ἕνα, ὃν ἐὰν εἴπητέ μοι κἀγὼ ὑμῖν ἐρῶ ἐν ποίᾳ ἐξουσίᾳ ταῦτα ποιῶ·
records.gloss: Answering then the Jesus said to them, Will ask you I also word one, which if you tell me, I also to you will say by what authority these things I do;
pieces: Jesus replied, "I too will put one question to you. If you answer it for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, then I will tell you by what authority I am doing these things.

L.24: And answering, Jesus said to them, "I also will ask you one question; if you tell {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} [the answer], I also will tell you by what authority I do these things.

R.24: Jesus answered, "I will ask you one question too. If you answer it, I will tell you what right I have to do these things.

decisions.choice: a question in return: a usual way of debate among teachers
decisions.reason: Answering a question with a question was a common way for teachers to argue. Jesus will answer if they do.

decisions.choice: word: here a question
decisions.reason: The noun has a wide range; the verb "ask" shows it means one question.

records.source: τὸ βάπτισμα τὸ Ἰωάννου πόθεν ἦν;
records.gloss: The baptism the of John from where was it?
pieces: John's baptism, where did it come from?

L.25: The baptism of John, where was it from?

R.25: Where did John's right to baptize come from?

decisions.choice: the baptism of John: his whole call to repent and be baptized
decisions.reason: John's baptism stands for his work as a prophet (3:1-12). The question is whether God sent him.

records.source: ἐξ οὐρανοῦ ἢ ἐξ ἀνθρώπων;
records.gloss: From heaven or from men?
pieces: Was it from heaven or from human beings?"

R.25: Did it come from God in heaven? Or did it come from people?"

decisions.choice: from heaven: from God
decisions.reason: Speaking of heaven was a reverent way to speak of God, as in "the kingdom of heaven".

decisions.choice: God in heaven
decisions.reason: Readable says that heaven stands for God.

records.source: οἱ δὲ διελογίζοντο ἐν ἑαυτοῖς λέγοντες· Ἐὰν εἴπωμεν· Ἐξ οὐρανοῦ, ἐρεῖ ἡμῖν· Διὰ τί οὖν οὐκ ἐπιστεύσατε αὐτῷ;
records.gloss: They then were reasoning among themselves saying, If we say, From heaven, he will say to us, Why then not did you believe him?
pieces: They began to argue it out among themselves: "If we say, 'From heaven,' {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will ask us, 'Then why did you not believe John?'

L.25: And they were reasoning among themselves, saying, "If we say, 'From heaven,' {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will say to us, 'Why then did you not believe him?'

R.25: The leaders talked about this among themselves. They said, "If we answer, 'From God in heaven,' Jesus will ask us, 'Then why did you not believe John?'

decisions.choice: reasoning among themselves: discussing it with one another
decisions.reason: The phrase can mean thinking within oneself, but they reason together as a group here.

decisions.choice: believe him: accept John's message as from God
alternatives: trust in John as a savior
decisions.reason: To believe John is to accept what he said, including what he said about the one coming after him (3:11).

decisions.choice: John
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say whom they did not believe.

records.source: ἐὰν δὲ εἴπωμεν· Ἐξ ἀνθρώπων, φοβούμεθα τὸν ὄχλον, πάντες γὰρ ὡς προφήτην ἔχουσιν τὸν Ἰωάννην.
records.gloss: If but we say, From men, we fear the crowd, all for as a prophet hold the John.
pieces: But if we say, 'From human beings,' we have the crowd to fear, since they all regard John as a prophet."

L.26: But if we say, 'From {{gender:people|men}},' we fear the crowd, for all hold John as a prophet."

R.26: But if we answer, 'From people,' then we have to worry about the crowd. Everyone thinks John was a prophet."

decisions.choice: the sentence breaks off: fear takes the place of the result
decisions.reason: They do not finish the thought "if we say this, then ...". They name their fear instead.

decisions.choice: they all hold John as a prophet: the people's high regard for John
decisions.reason: Crowds from all Judea had gone out to John (3:5). Jesus himself called him a prophet and more (11:9).

records.source: καὶ ἀποκριθέντες τῷ Ἰησοῦ εἶπαν· Οὐκ οἴδαμεν.
records.gloss: And answering Jesus they said, Not we know.
pieces: So they answered Jesus, "We do not know."

L.27: And answering Jesus, they said, "We do not know."

R.27: So they answered Jesus, "We do not know."

decisions.choice: we do not know: a refusal to answer
alternatives: a real admission that they did not know
decisions.reason: Their reasoning in 21:25-26 shows that they choose not to commit themselves.

records.source: ἔφη αὐτοῖς καὶ αὐτός· Οὐδὲ ἐγὼ λέγω ὑμῖν ἐν ποίᾳ ἐξουσίᾳ ταῦτα ποιῶ.
records.gloss: Said to them also he, Neither I tell you by what authority these things I do.
pieces: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to them, "Then I will not tell you either by what authority I do these things.

L.27: He also said to them, "Neither do I tell you by what authority I do these things.

R.27: Jesus said, "Then I will not tell you either what right I have to do these things.

decisions.choice: neither do I tell you: Jesus will not answer those who will not answer
decisions.reason: Jesus keeps the bargain of 21:24. The parables that follow still show where he stands.

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: Readable names Jesus.

records.source: Τί δὲ ὑμῖν δοκεῖ;
records.gloss: What but to you seems?
pieces: Now tell me what you think.

R.28: What do you think about this?

decisions.choice: what do you think: an invitation to judge the story
decisions.reason: Jesus asks his hearers to give a verdict, as he does in 18:12 and 22:42. Their answer will judge them (21:31).

records.heading: Two sons and their father's will

records.source: ἄνθρωπος εἶχεν τέκνα δύο.
records.gloss: A man had children two.
pieces: A man had two sons.

R.28: There was a man who had two sons.

decisions.choice: children: here two sons
decisions.reason: The word means children, but the forms in 21:29-30 show both are sons.

decisions.choice: children (L); sons (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the general word; Balanced and Readable say what the story shows.

decisions.choice: no spans for the father
alternatives: spans on he and his for the father
decisions.reason: The father is a figure in a parable, so his pronouns take no deity_pronoun span.

records.source: προσελθὼν τῷ πρώτῳ εἶπεν· Τέκνον, ὕπαγε σήμερον ἐργάζου ἐν τῷ ἀμπελῶνι.
records.gloss: Having come to the first he said, Child, go today work in the vineyard.
pieces: He came to the first one and said, 'Go and work in the vineyard today, son.'

L.28: Coming to the first, he said, 'Child, go today, work in the vineyard.'

R.28: The father went to the first son and said, 'Son, go and work in the vineyard today.'

decisions.choice: child: a father's warm address to his son
decisions.reason: The word is used as a kindly address (9:2).

decisions.choice: the vineyard: a familiar picture of God's people and his work
decisions.reason: Israel is God's vineyard in Isaiah 5:1-7, and 20:1-16 pictured work in a vineyard. The picture returns in 21:33.

records.source: ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν· Οὐ θέλω· ὕστερον δὲ μεταμεληθεὶς ἀπῆλθεν.
records.gloss: He then answering said, Not I want; later then having regretted he went.
pieces: He answered, 'I do not want to.' Yet afterward he changed his mind and went.

L.29: And answering, he said, 'I do not want to'; but later, having changed his mind, he went.

R.29: The son answered, 'I will not go.' But later he was sorry. He changed his mind and went to work.

decisions.choice: the first son refuses and then goes; the second agrees and does not go: the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: the order reversed, with the first son agreeing and not going, and the answer "the last" in 21:31
the order of the SBLGNT, but with the answer "the last"
decisions.reason: Manuscripts tell this parable in three forms. Some important early ones reverse the two sons and have the answer "the last". A few others keep this order but give the answer "the last", which makes the leaders answer wrongly. The meaning of the parable is the same in the first two forms. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: changed his mind: regretted his answer and turned around
decisions.reason: The verb means to regret and change course. Jesus uses it again in 21:32 of those who did not change their minds and believe.

decisions.choice: he was sorry. He changed his mind
decisions.reason: Readable gives both sides of the verb: regret and a change of course.

records.source: προσελθὼν δὲ τῷ δευτέρῳ εἶπεν ὡσαύτως· ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν· Ἐγώ, κύριε· καὶ οὐκ ἀπῆλθεν.
records.gloss: Having come then to the second he said likewise. He then answering said, I, sir; and not he went.
pieces: Then the father went to the second son and said the same thing. This one answered, 'I will, sir,' but he did not go.

L.30: And coming to the second, he said the same. And answering, he said, 'I [go], sir,' and he did not go.

R.30: Then the father went to the other son and told him the same thing. This son answered, 'Yes, sir, I will go.' But he did not go.

decisions.choice: I, sir: a short and polite yes, with the verb understood
decisions.reason: The reply has only "I" and the address. It means "I will go, sir".

decisions.choice: sir: the respectful address to a father or master
alternatives: Lord, as an address to God
decisions.reason: The same word is used for the Lord; here it is a son's respectful word to his father.

decisions.choice: the father; son
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say who spoke to whom.

records.source: τίς ἐκ τῶν δύο ἐποίησεν τὸ θέλημα τοῦ πατρός;
records.gloss: Which of the two did the will of the father?
pieces: Which of the two did what their father wanted?"

L.31: Which of the two did the will of the father?"

R.31: Which of the two sons did what his father wanted?"

decisions.choice: doing the will of the father: the test Jesus gave in 7:21
alternatives: only a son's duty at home
decisions.reason: Not everyone who says "Lord" will enter the kingdom, but the one who does the will of the Father (7:21; 12:50).

decisions.choice: did what their father wanted (B); did what his father wanted (R)
alternatives: did the will of the father
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable put the phrase in plain words.

records.source: λέγουσιν· Ὁ πρῶτος.
records.gloss: They say, The first.
pieces: "The first," they answered.

decisions.choice: the first, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: the last, in manuscripts that reverse the sons
the last, in a few manuscripts that keep this order
decisions.reason: See the note on 21:29. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: present tense of narration (L); past (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek present tense of narration.

records.source: λέγει αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι οἱ τελῶναι καὶ αἱ πόρναι προάγουσιν ὑμᾶς εἰς τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ θεοῦ.
records.gloss: Says to them the Jesus, Truly I say to you that the tax collectors and the prostitutes go before you into the kingdom of the God.
pieces: Jesus said to them, "Truly I tell you, the tax collectors and the prostitutes are leading the way into the kingdom of God, ahead of you.

L.31: Jesus says to them, "Truly I tell you that the tax collectors and the prostitutes are going ahead of you into the kingdom of God.

R.31: Jesus said to them, "I tell you the truth. Tax collectors and prostitutes are going into God's kingdom before you.

decisions.choice: are going ahead of you: they enter first, and the leaders have not yet entered
decisions.reason: The verb means to go before someone. It leaves the door open for the leaders, though 21:43 warns that the kingdom will be taken from them.

decisions.choice: tax collectors and prostitutes: people the devout counted as beyond hope
decisions.reason: Tax collectors worked for the rulers and were known for cheating (9:10-11). Prostitutes lived plainly against the law. Both are named as those who believed John (21:32).

decisions.choice: present tense of narration (L); past (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek present tense of narration.

decisions.choice: God's kingdom
decisions.reason: Readable uses the shorter form, as in 4:23.

records.source: ἦλθεν γὰρ Ἰωάννης πρὸς ὑμᾶς ἐν ὁδῷ δικαιοσύνης, καὶ οὐκ ἐπιστεύσατε αὐτῷ· οἱ δὲ τελῶναι καὶ αἱ πόρναι ἐπίστευσαν αὐτῷ· ὑμεῖς δὲ ἰδόντες οὐδὲ μετεμελήθητε ὕστερον τοῦ πιστεῦσαι αὐτῷ.
records.gloss: Came for John to you in way of righteousness, and not you believed him; the but tax collectors and the prostitutes believed him; you but having seen not even regretted afterward to believe him.
pieces: For John came to you showing the way of righteousness, and you did not believe him. But the tax collectors and the prostitutes did believe him. And even after you saw that, you did not change your minds later and believe him.

L.32: For John came to you in [the] way of righteousness, and you did not believe him, but the tax collectors and the prostitutes believed him; and you, having seen [it], did not even change your minds afterward to believe him.

R.32: John came to show you the righteous way to live, and you did not believe him. But the tax collectors and prostitutes believed him. You saw this happen. But even then you did not change your minds and believe him.

decisions.choice: in the way of righteousness: living and teaching the right way before God
alternatives: only in a righteous manner of life
decisions.reason: John both lived rightly and called people to the life God requires (3:2-12). Jesus said that he and John were to fulfill all righteousness (3:15).

decisions.choice: change your minds: the same verb as the first son's change in 21:29
alternatives: repent of all sin in general
decisions.reason: The leaders are like the second son. They said yes to God but did not turn when John came, even when they saw sinners turn.

decisions.choice: to believe him: the change they did not make was believing
decisions.reason: The infinitive tells what changing their minds would have meant: coming to believe John.

decisions.choice: the righteous way to live
decisions.reason: Readable keeps the key word in its adjective form and says what the way was.

records.source: Ἄλλην παραβολὴν ἀκούσατε.
records.gloss: Another parable hear.
pieces: Listen to another parable.

decisions.choice: parable: a story that compares and teaches
decisions.reason: As in chapter 13, a parable sets a picture beside the truth it teaches.

decisions.choice: story
decisions.reason: Readable uses a plain word for a teaching story.

records.heading: The tenants who killed the owner's son

records.source: Ἄνθρωπος ἦν οἰκοδεσπότης ὅστις ἐφύτευσεν ἀμπελῶνα καὶ φραγμὸν αὐτῷ περιέθηκεν καὶ ὤρυξεν ἐν αὐτῷ ληνὸν καὶ ᾠκοδόμησεν πύργον, καὶ ἐξέδετο αὐτὸν γεωργοῖς, καὶ ἀπεδήμησεν.
records.gloss: A man there was a master of a house who planted a vineyard and a fence it placed around and dug in it a winepress and built a tower, and rented out it to farmers, and traveled abroad.
pieces: A man who owned an estate planted a vineyard. He set a hedge around it, cut a pit for a winepress, and put up a watchtower. Then he leased it to tenant farmers and went abroad.

L.33: There was a man, a master of a house, who planted a vineyard and put a fence around it and dug a winepress in it and built a tower, and leased it to farmers and went abroad.

R.33: A man owned some land, and he planted grapevines on it. He put a fence around the vineyard. He dug out a place to crush the grapes. He built a tall tower so a guard could watch over it. Then he let some farmers use the vineyard and pay him rent. After that he went away to another country.

decisions.choice: planting, fence, winepress, tower: Isaiah 5:1-2
decisions.reason: Isaiah sings of a vineyard its owner prepared in just this way. There the vineyard is the house of Israel and the owner is the LORD (Isaiah 5:7). Jesus' hearers would know the song.

decisions.choice: leased it to farmers: tenants who worked the land and paid the owner part of the crop
alternatives: hired laborers paid by the day
decisions.reason: Landowners who lived far away often let land to tenant farmers, who paid rent in produce.

decisions.choice: winepress: a pit cut in the rock to tread grapes
decisions.reason: Grapes were trodden in a shallow basin, and the juice ran into a lower pit, as the verb "dug" shows.

decisions.choice: no spans for the owner or his son
alternatives: spans because they stand for God and Jesus
decisions.reason: The owner and his son are figures in a parable, so their pronouns take no deity_pronoun span, like the sower and the master in other parables.

decisions.choice: tenant farmers (B); farmers who use the vineyard and pay him rent (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable show that the farmers were tenants.

records.source: ὅτε δὲ ἤγγισεν ὁ καιρὸς τῶν καρπῶν, ἀπέστειλεν τοὺς δούλους αὐτοῦ πρὸς τοὺς γεωργοὺς λαβεῖν τοὺς καρποὺς αὐτοῦ.
records.gloss: When then drew near the season of the fruits, he sent the slaves of him to the farmers to receive the fruits of him.
pieces: When harvest time came near, he sent his servants to the tenants to collect his share of the crop.

L.34: And when the season of the fruits drew near, he sent his slaves to the farmers to receive his fruits.

R.34: When it was time to pick the grapes, the owner sent his servants to the farmers to get his share of the grapes.

decisions.choice: slaves: the owner's slaves, sent with his authority
decisions.reason: The word means a slave, a person owned by a master. The prophets are called God's slaves (Jeremiah 7:25; Amos 3:7), and the story points to them.

decisions.choice: his fruits: the share of the crop that belonged to the owner
decisions.reason: The pronoun most naturally refers to the owner. Under a lease he was owed part of the harvest.

decisions.choice: his share of the crop (B); his share of the grapes (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the owner was owed.

decisions.choice: servants
decisions.reason: "Servant" in Balanced and Readable, as the style guide has it; the meaning decision (m1) keeps that they were owned, and Literal keeps "slave".

records.source: καὶ λαβόντες οἱ γεωργοὶ τοὺς δούλους αὐτοῦ ὃν μὲν ἔδειραν, ὃν δὲ ἀπέκτειναν, ὃν δὲ ἐλιθοβόλησαν.
records.gloss: And having taken the farmers the slaves of him, one they beat, another they killed, another they stoned.
pieces: The tenants grabbed his servants. One they beat up, another they killed, and another they pelted with stones.

L.35: And the farmers, taking his slaves, beat one, killed another, and stoned another.

R.35: But the farmers grabbed the owner's servants. They beat one of them. They killed another one. And they threw stones at another one.

decisions.choice: beaten, killed, stoned: the way the prophets were treated
alternatives: violence with no meaning beyond the story
decisions.reason: Zechariah son of Jehoiada was stoned in the temple court (2 Chronicles 24:21), and Jesus will speak of Jerusalem stoning those sent to her (23:37).

decisions.choice: stoned: pelted with stones, often to death
decisions.reason: Stoning was a way of putting someone to death, but the verb itself means to throw stones at someone.

decisions.choice: servants
decisions.reason: "Servant" in Balanced and Readable, as the style guide has it, and Literal keeps "slave".

records.source: πάλιν ἀπέστειλεν ἄλλους δούλους πλείονας τῶν πρώτων, καὶ ἐποίησαν αὐτοῖς ὡσαύτως.
records.gloss: Again he sent other slaves more than the first, and they did to them likewise.
pieces: So the owner sent other servants, a larger group than the first, and the tenants treated them the same way.

L.36: Again he sent other slaves, more than the first, and they did the same to them.

R.36: So the owner sent more servants, more than the first time. But the farmers did the same things to them.

decisions.choice: more than the first: more in number
decisions.reason: The word can mean greater in number or in rank. Here more slaves are sent.

decisions.choice: the owner; the tenants (B), the farmers (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name who sent and who acted.

decisions.choice: servants
decisions.reason: "Servant" in Balanced and Readable, as the style guide has it, and Literal keeps "slave".

records.source: ὕστερον δὲ ἀπέστειλεν πρὸς αὐτοὺς τὸν υἱὸν αὐτοῦ λέγων· Ἐντραπήσονται τὸν υἱόν μου.
records.gloss: Last then he sent to them the son of him saying, They will respect the son of me.
pieces: Finally he sent his son to them. He told himself, 'They will show respect to my son.'

L.37: And later he sent his son to them, saying, 'They will respect my son.'

R.37: Finally the owner sent his son to them. He thought, 'The farmers will respect my son.'

decisions.choice: his son: in the story, the owner's son; in its meaning, Jesus
decisions.reason: The son comes after all the slaves and is the heir (21:38). God has called Jesus his beloved Son (3:17), and the leaders see that the story is about them (21:45).

decisions.choice: later: at last, after all the others
decisions.reason: The word means afterward or finally; the son is the last one sent.

decisions.choice: respect: feel shame before, and so treat with honor
decisions.reason: The verb means to turn back in shame before someone, and so to show them respect.

decisions.choice: He told himself (B); He thought (R)
decisions.reason: The owner speaks his hope rather than giving an order, so Balanced and Readable make it his thought.

records.source: οἱ δὲ γεωργοὶ ἰδόντες τὸν υἱὸν εἶπον ἐν ἑαυτοῖς· Οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ κληρονόμος· δεῦτε ἀποκτείνωμεν αὐτὸν καὶ σχῶμεν τὴν κληρονομίαν αὐτοῦ·
records.gloss: The but farmers having seen the son said among themselves, This is the heir; come let us kill him and let us have the inheritance of him;
pieces: The tenants, though, saw the son and said to one another, 'Here is the one who will inherit the vineyard. Come on, if we kill him, his inheritance will be ours.'

L.38: But the farmers, seeing the son, said among themselves, 'This is the heir; come, let us kill him and have his inheritance.'

R.38: But when the farmers saw the son, they talked among themselves. They said, 'This son will own the vineyard someday. Let us kill him! Then the vineyard will belong to us.'

decisions.choice: kill the heir and take the inheritance: a scheme to keep the land
decisions.reason: With the heir dead and the owner far away, the tenants hope the land will be left to those who hold it.

decisions.choice: come, let us kill him: the words of Joseph's brothers
decisions.reason: Joseph's brothers said almost the same when they saw him coming (Genesis 37:20 in the Greek Old Testament).

decisions.choice: the vineyard
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the son would inherit.

records.source: καὶ λαβόντες αὐτὸν ἐξέβαλον ἔξω τοῦ ἀμπελῶνος καὶ ἀπέκτειναν.
records.gloss: And having taken him they cast out outside of the vineyard and killed.
pieces: They took hold of him, forced him outside the vineyard, and killed him.

L.39: And taking him, they threw [him] out of the vineyard and killed [him].

R.39: So they grabbed the son and threw him out of the vineyard. Then they killed him.

decisions.choice: thrown out and then killed: the son dies outside the vineyard
decisions.reason: Mark 12:8 has the son killed and then thrown out. Matthew's order may look ahead to Jesus' death outside the city (27:31-33; Hebrews 13:12).

records.source: ὅταν οὖν ἔλθῃ ὁ κύριος τοῦ ἀμπελῶνος, τί ποιήσει τοῖς γεωργοῖς ἐκείνοις;
records.gloss: When therefore comes the lord of the vineyard, what will he do to the farmers those?
pieces: Now when the owner of the vineyard comes, what will he do to those tenants?"

L.40: So when the master of the vineyard comes, what will he do to those farmers?"

R.40: So what will the owner of the vineyard do to those farmers when he comes back?"

decisions.choice: master: the owner of the vineyard
decisions.reason: The word is the one used for the Lord, but in the story it means the owner. It hints at who the owner stands for.

decisions.choice: what will he do: Jesus lets the hearers pass judgment
decisions.reason: As in 21:28-31, the hearers give the verdict. They answer in 21:41.

records.source: λέγουσιν αὐτῷ· Κακοὺς κακῶς ἀπολέσει αὐτούς, καὶ τὸν ἀμπελῶνα ἐκδώσεται ἄλλοις γεωργοῖς, οἵτινες ἀποδώσουσιν αὐτῷ τοὺς καρποὺς ἐν τοῖς καιροῖς αὐτῶν.
records.gloss: They say to him, Bad men badly he will destroy them, and the vineyard he will rent out to other farmers, who will give to him the fruits in the seasons of them.
pieces: They answered {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "He will put those evil men to a miserable death, and he will lease the vineyard to other tenants, who will hand over the fruit to him at each harvest."

L.41: They say to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "[Those] wretches he will destroy wretchedly, and he will lease the vineyard to other farmers, who will give him the fruits in their seasons."

R.41: They answered {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "He will kill those evil men in a terrible way. Then he will rent the vineyard to other farmers. They will give him his share of the grapes at harvest time."

decisions.choice: bad men badly: a play on words, the evil end of evil men
decisions.reason: The adjective and the adverb come from the same word. The punishment matches the crime.

decisions.choice: the hearers pronounce their own sentence
decisions.reason: The chief priests and elders (21:23) give the verdict on the tenants before they see that the story is about them (21:45), as David did before Nathan (2 Samuel 12:5-7).

decisions.choice: present tense of narration (L); past (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek present tense of narration.

decisions.choice: put those evil men to a miserable death (B); kill those evil men in a terrible way (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable keep the link between the men and their end without the repeated word.

records.source: Λέγει αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Οὐδέποτε ἀνέγνωτε ἐν ταῖς γραφαῖς· Λίθον ὃν ἀπεδοκίμασαν οἱ οἰκοδομοῦντες οὗτος ἐγενήθη εἰς κεφαλὴν γωνίας· παρὰ κυρίου ἐγένετο αὕτη, καὶ ἔστιν θαυμαστὴ ἐν ὀφθαλμοῖς ἡμῶν;
records.gloss: Says to them the Jesus, Never did you read in the Scriptures, A stone which rejected the building ones, this became into head of corner; from Lord came this, and it is marvelous in eyes of us?
pieces: Jesus said to them, "Did you never read this in the Scriptures: 'The very stone the builders turned down has become the cornerstone. The Lord has brought this about, and we look on it with wonder'?

L.42: Jesus says to them, "Have you never read in the Scriptures, '[The] stone that the builders rejected, this has become [the] head of [the] corner; from [the] Lord this came about, and it is marvelous in our eyes'?

R.42: Jesus said to them, "Surely you have read this in the Scriptures: 'The stone that the builders did not want has become the most important stone in the building. The Lord did this, and it is wonderful to us.'

decisions.reason: The words come from the same psalm the crowds sang in 21:9. Where Matthew has "Lord", the Hebrew has God's name, the LORD.

decisions.choice: the rejected stone: Jesus, rejected by the leaders and made chief by God
decisions.reason: The builders are the leaders who reject the son, as in the parable. Peter applies the verse to Jesus' death and resurrection (Acts 4:11; 1 Peter 2:7).

decisions.choice: head of the corner: the main stone that holds the corner
alternatives: the top stone over an arch
decisions.reason: The phrase can mean a cornerstone at the base or a capstone at the top. Either way it is the stone the whole building depends on.

decisions.choice: this came from the Lord: God has done it
alternatives: the stone came from the Lord
decisions.reason: "This" refers to the whole turn of events, the rejected stone becoming the chief one.

decisions.choice: present tense of narration (L); past (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek present tense of narration.

decisions.choice: a statement instead of a question
decisions.reason: The question expects yes; Readable states it, as in 21:16.

records.source: διὰ τοῦτο λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι ἀρθήσεται ἀφ’ ὑμῶν ἡ βασιλεία τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ δοθήσεται ἔθνει ποιοῦντι τοὺς καρποὺς αὐτῆς.
records.gloss: Because of this I say to you that will be taken away from you the kingdom of the God and it will be given to a people producing the fruits of it.
pieces: This is why I tell you: you will lose the kingdom of God. It will be taken from you and given to a people that bears the fruit it calls for.

L.43: Because of this I tell you that the kingdom of God will be taken away from you and will be given to a people producing its fruits.

R.43: So I tell you this: God's kingdom will be taken away from you. It will be given to people who produce the fruit it should have.

decisions.choice: a people: a new community that does God's will
alternatives: the Gentiles in place of Israel
decisions.reason: The word is often used of nations. Here it is the people, of any background, who bear the kingdom's fruit, like the tax collectors who believed (21:31-32).

decisions.choice: its fruits: the deeds the kingdom calls for
decisions.reason: Fruit is a picture of a life that matches repentance (3:8; 7:16-20), the fruit the owner came to collect (21:34).

decisions.choice: will be taken away from you: from the leaders who are listening
decisions.reason: Jesus speaks to the chief priests and elders (21:23), and they know he means them (21:45).

decisions.choice: God's kingdom
decisions.reason: Readable uses the shorter form.

records.source: Καὶ ὁ πεσὼν ἐπὶ τὸν λίθον τοῦτον συνθλασθήσεται· ἐφ’ ὃν δ’ ἂν πέσῃ λικμήσει αὐτόν.
records.gloss: And the having fallen on the stone this will be broken to pieces; on whomever but it may fall, it will crush him.
pieces: Whoever falls on this stone will be dashed to pieces, and if it falls on anyone, it will crush {{gender:them|him}} to dust."

L.44: And the one who falls on this stone will be broken to pieces; and on whomever it falls, it will crush {{gender:them|him}}."

R.44: Anyone who falls on this stone will be broken into pieces. And if the stone falls on someone, it will crush that person."

decisions.choice: the verse is included, as in the SBLGNT
alternatives: the verse is left out, as in some manuscripts
decisions.reason: A few early witnesses lack this verse, and some think it was added from Luke 20:18, which is very similar. Most manuscripts, including important early ones, have it. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: the stone that breaks and crushes: Isaiah 8:14-15 and Daniel 2:34-35, 44-45
decisions.reason: In Isaiah the LORD is a stone over which many stumble and are broken. In Daniel a stone not cut by human hands crushes the kingdoms of the world.

decisions.choice: crush: grind to powder, scatter like chaff
decisions.reason: The verb was used of winnowing grain. The Greek Old Testament uses it in Daniel 2:44 of God's kingdom crushing all others.

records.source: Καὶ ἀκούσαντες οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ οἱ Φαρισαῖοι τὰς παραβολὰς αὐτοῦ ἔγνωσαν ὅτι περὶ αὐτῶν λέγει·
records.gloss: And having heard the chief priests and the Pharisees the parables of him they knew that about them he speaks;
pieces: The chief priests and the Pharisees heard {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} parables and realized that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} meant them.

L.45: And when the chief priests and the Pharisees heard {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} parables, they knew that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was speaking about them.

R.45: The leading priests and the Pharisees heard the stories Jesus told. They knew {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was talking about them.

decisions.choice: his parables: the two sons and the tenants, and perhaps the stone
decisions.reason: The plural takes in the stories just told in the temple.

decisions.choice: he was speaking: present in the Greek, as reported thought
decisions.reason: Greek keeps the tense of the original thought: "he is speaking about us".

decisions.choice: the stories Jesus told
decisions.reason: Readable uses "stories" for parables, as in 21:33, and names Jesus.

records.source: καὶ ζητοῦντες αὐτὸν κρατῆσαι ἐφοβήθησαν τοὺς ὄχλους, ἐπεὶ εἰς προφήτην αὐτὸν εἶχον.
records.gloss: And seeking him to seize they feared the crowds, since as a prophet him they were holding.
pieces: They wanted to arrest {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, but they were afraid of the crowds, who regarded {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} as a prophet.

L.46: And seeking to seize {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, they feared the crowds, because they held {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} as a prophet.

R.46: They wanted to arrest Jesus. But they were afraid of the crowds, because the people thought {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was a prophet.

decisions.choice: seeking to seize him: they wanted to arrest him but held back
decisions.reason: The participle gives their aim; their fear of the crowds kept them from acting then (see 26:4-5).

decisions.choice: held him as a prophet: the same regard the crowds had for John
alternatives: they thought he was the Messiah
decisions.reason: The leaders fear the crowds over Jesus just as they feared them over John (21:26). The crowds called him the prophet in 21:11.
